## Proposed Wave 141A design (Voice 3 architect refines)

### A. settings.json `permissions.allow[]` Docker class additions (~12-15 entries)

Add Bash(docker run *) / Bash(docker exec *) / Bash(docker ps *) / Bash(docker stop *) /

Bash(docker compose *) / Bash(docker network *) / Bash(docker volume ls *) /

Bash(docker mcp *) / Bash(docker agent *)

Each entry cite-anchored at `https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/<subcommand>/`
or upstream `docker/cli` source.

### B. safety_guard.py Docker policy extension (~5-7 NEW deny patterns)

KEEP existing `docker system prune` regex. ADD:
- `docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq)` (remove ALL incl running)
- `docker rmi $(docker images -q)` (remove ALL images)
- `docker run --privileged` (host-namespace escape)
- `docker run --net=host` / `docker run --net host` (host network bypass)
- `docker run --pid=host` / `docker run --pid host` (host PID bypass)
- `docker exec --privileged` (privileged exec)
- `docker plugin install` (third-party kernel-level plugin attack surface)

While most Docker commands are short-lived (running for seconds or minutes), the `docker mcp gateway run` command creates a long-running process that maintains persistent connections with AI clients. The Wasm microservice is an HTTP API connected to a MySQL (MariaDB) database. The API is invoked via from JavaScript in a web interface serving static HTML. The microservice is compiled into WebAssembly (Wasm) and runs in the WasmEdge Runtime, a secure and lightweight alternative to natively compiled Rust apps in Linux containers. Z:\repos\deps\docker-agent\docs\features\skills\index.md:109:By default, when an agent invokes a skill it reads the instructions inline into its own conversation. Z:\repos\deps\docker-agent\docs\features\skills\index.md:111:Adding `context: fork` to the SKILL.md frontmatter tells the agent to run the skill in an **isolated sub-agent** instead:
Z:\repos\deps\docker-agent\docs\features\skills\index.md:118:context: fork
Z:\repos\deps\docker-agent\docs\features\skills\index.md:128:When the agent encounters a task that matches a `context: fork` skill, it uses the `run_skill` tool instead of `read_skill`. This:
Z:\repos\deps\docker-agent\docs\features\skills\index.md:131:- **Isolates the context window** — the sub-agent has its own conversation history, so lengthy tool-call chains don't eat into the parent's token budget

# 🤖 Docker Agent 🤖

> Build, run, and share AI agents with a declarative YAML config, rich tool ecosystem, and multi-agent orchestration.

![docker agent in action](docs/demo.gif)

## What is Docker Agent?

`docker-agent` lets you create and run intelligent AI agents that collaborate to solve complex problems — no code required.

`docker-agent` is a `docker` CLI plugin and can be run with `docker agent`.

Define agents in YAML, give them tools, and let them work.

```yaml
agents:
  root:
    model: openai/gpt-5-mini
    description: A helpful AI assistant
    instruction: |
      You are a knowledgeable assistant that helps users with various tasks.
      Be helpful, accurate, and concise in your responses.
    toolsets:
      - type: mcp
        ref: docker:duckduckgo
```

```sh
docker agent run agent.yaml
```

## Key Features

- **Multi-agent architecture** — Create teams of specialized agents that delegate tasks automatically
- **Rich tool ecosystem** — Built-in tools + any [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server (local, remote, or Docker-based)
- **AI provider agnostic** — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, xAI, [Docker Model Runner](https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner/), and more
- **YAML configuration** — Declarative, versionable, shareable
- **Advanced reasoning** — Built-in think, todo, and memory tools
- **RAG** — Pluggable retrieval with BM25, embeddings, hybrid search, and reranking
- **Package & share** — Push agents to any OCI registry, pull and run them anywhere

## Install

**Docker Desktop** (4.63+) — docker-agent CLI plugin is pre-installed. Just run `docker agent`.

**Homebrew** — `brew install docker-agent`. Run `docker-agent` directly or symlink the binary to `~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent` and run `docker agent`.

**Binary releases** — Download from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/docker/docker-agent/releases). Symlink the `docker-agent` binary to `~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent` to be able to use `docker agent`, or use `docker-agent` directly.

Set at least one API key (or use [Docker Model Runner](https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner/) for local models):

```sh
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...        # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, etc.
```

## Quick Start

```sh
# Run the default agent
docker agent run

# Run from the agent catalog
docker agent run agentcatalog/pirate

# Generate a new agent interactively
docker agent new

# Run your own config
docker agent run agent.yaml
```

More examples in the [`examples/`](examples/README.md) directory.

# Docker MCP Plugin and Docker MCP Gateway

![build](https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)

The [MCP Toolkit](https://docs.docker.com/ai/mcp-catalog-and-toolkit/toolkit/), in Docker Desktop, allows
developers to configure and consume MCP servers from the [Docker MCP Catalog](https://hub.docker.com/mcp).

Underneath, the Toolkit is powered by a docker CLI plugin: `docker-mcp`. This repository is the code of this CLI plugin. It can work in Docker Desktop or independently.

The main feature of this CLI is the **Docker MCP Gateway** which allows easy and secure running and deployment of MCP servers. See [Features](#Features) for a list of all the features.

## What is MCP?

The [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/) is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect to external data sources and tools. It provides a secure, controlled way for language models to access and interact with various services, databases, and APIs.

## Overview

Developers face criticial barriers when integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools into production workflows:

- **Managing MCP server lifecycle** Each local MCP sever in the catalog runs in an isolated Docker container. npx and uvx servers are granted minimal host privileges.
- **Providing a unified interface** AI models access MCP servers through a single Gateway.
- **Handling authentication and security** Keep secrets out of environment variables using Docker Desktop's secrets management.
- **Supports dynamic tool discovery** and configuration. Each MCP client (eg VS Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, etc.) connects to the same Gateway configuration, ensuring consistency across different clients.
- **Enables OAuth flows** for MCPs that require OAuth access token service connections.

## Features

- 🐳 **Container-based Servers**: Run MCP servers as Docker containers with proper isolation.
- 🔧 **Server Management**: List, inspect, and call MCP tools, resources and prompts from multiple servers.
- 🔐 **Secrets Management**: Secure handling of API keys and credentials via Docker Desktop.
- 🌐 **OAuth Integration**: Built-in OAuth flows for service authentication.
- 📋 **Server Catalog**: Manage and configure multiple MCP catalogs.
- 🔍 **Dynamic Discovery**: Automatic tool, prompt, and resource discovery from running servers.
- 📊 **Monitoring**: Built-in logging and call tracing capabilities.

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Docker Desktop `4.59+` (with MCP Toolkit feature enabled)

<div align="left">
  <img src="./img/enable_toolkit.png" width="400"/>
</div>
- Go 1.24+ (for development)

### Install as Docker CLI Plugin

The MCP cli will already be installed on recent versions of Docker Desktop but you can build and install the latest version by following these steps:

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway.git
cd mcp-gateway
mkdir -p "$HOME/.docker/cli-plugins/"

# Build and install the plugin
make docker-mcp
```

After installation, the plugin will be available as:

```bash
docker mcp --help
```

## Usage

> [!NOTE]
> **Running without Docker Desktop Feature Flags**
>
> If you encounter "Docker Desktop is not running" errors when the Docker daemon is active, you can bypass Desktop feature checks by setting:
> ```bash
> export DOCKER_MCP_IN_CONTAINER=1
> ```
> This is useful when running in WSL2, containerized environments, or Docker CE where Desktop backend sockets are unavailable.

> [!NOTE]
> **Enabling Profiles outside Docker Desktop**
>
> Profiles are enabled automatically in Docker Desktop. If you are using the CLI independently (e.g. Docker CE, WSL2, or a containerized environment), enable the profiles feature first:
> ```bash
> docker mcp feature enable profiles
> ```

### Profile Management

Servers are organized into **profiles**. A profile groups related MCP servers together and can be connected to clients, exported, and shared via OCI registries.

Servers in a profile can reference multiple sources:
- **Catalog references**: `catalog://mcp/docker-mcp-catalog/github`
- **OCI image references**: `docker://my-server:latest`
- **MCP Registry references**: `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers/<id>`
- **Local file references**: `file://./server.yaml`

```bash
# Make sure to `docker mcp catalog pull mcp/docker-mcp-catalog` first.

# Create a new profile
docker mcp profile create --name dev-tools \
  --server catalog://mcp/docker-mcp-catalog/github

# Create a profile and connect it to a client
docker mcp profile create --name dev-tools \
  --server catalog://mcp/docker-mcp-catalog/github \
  --connect cursor

# List all profiles
docker mcp profile list

# Show profile details
docker mcp profile show <profile-id>

# Remove a profile
docker mcp profile remove <profile-id>

# Export/import profiles
docker mcp profile export <profile-id> output.yaml
docker mcp profile import input.yaml

"""PreToolUse safety-guard — intercept destructive Bash commands.

Contract:
- stdin JSON: {"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "..."}}
- exit 0: allow (proceed)
- exit 2: block (stderr message shown to Claude with reason + suggested alternative)
- fail-CLOSED on safety-gate corruption: stdin read failure / malformed JSON / evaluate() exception -> exit 2
  (closed by Ship 29.A.2 per Wave 29 Agent A REAL GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE BLOCK + T3 R1 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.86 monotone-decline path)
- fail-open preserved on explicit allow paths: empty stdin / tool_name != "Bash" / empty command (no-command-to-check semantic)

Patterns matched (Careful Mode per ECC safety-guard SKILL.md):
  rm -rf / | rm -rf /* | rm -rf ~ | rm -rf * | rm -rf .
  sudo rm
  git push --force / -f
  git reset --hard
  git checkout .
  DROP TABLE / DATABASE / SCHEMA / INDEX (any case)
  TRUNCATE TABLE (any case)
  docker system prune
  kubectl delete
  chmod 777
  :(){ :|:& };: (fork bomb)
  mkfs.* (filesystem format)
  dd to /dev/[sh]d* (raw disk overwrite)
  --no-verify (always-block, overlaps with block_no_verify_guard)

Three-layer scan:
  1. Whole-command scan (fork-bomb class only — patterns containing `;`/`|` that
     per-sub splitter would fragment). Quote-stripped via _strip_quoted_regions.
  2. Per-sub scan: split on `;`/`&&`/`||`/newlines/`|`. For each sub:
     a. ALWAYS_BLOCK patterns fire even inside _DATA_PREFIXES (e.g. --no-verify
        inside `git commit` still blocks because the flag actually skips hooks).
        Exempted by _ALWAYS_BLOCK_EXEMPT_PREFIXES (echo/printf/grep/rg/cat/awk/
        sed/less/more — text tools where args are pure data).
     b. _DATA_PREFIXES (git commit / echo / printf / gh issue/pr/etc / heredoc) —
        skip pattern match because args are data, not subcommands.
     c. _DESTRUCTIVE patterns scanned against per-sub.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

_HOOKS_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
if str(_HOOKS_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_HOOKS_DIR))

try:
    from utils import log_swallow
except ImportError:
    def log_swallow(exc: Exception, context: str) -> None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"[safety-guard:fallback] {context}: {exc}\n")


# Each pattern: (regex, human-readable description, suggested safer alternative)
# Keep patterns narrow to avoid false-positives (legitimate `git reset` non-hard, etc.)
_DESTRUCTIVE: tuple[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str, str], ...] = (
    # rm -rf followed by ONE of: standalone `/`, `~`, `*`, `/*`, or `.` (as whole argument)
    (re.compile(r"\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*[rRfF][a-zA-Z]*\s+)+(/|~|\*|/\*|\.)(?=\s|$|;|\||&)"),
     "rm -rf against root/home/wildcard/glob/cwd",
     "specify an exact path; consider `git clean -fd` for tracked-file cleanup"),
    (re.compile(r"\bsudo\s+rm\b"),
     "sudo rm (elevated destructive delete)",
     "avoid sudo for file removal; drop privileges if possible"),
    (re.compile(r"\bgit\s+push\s+.*(--force\b|--force-with-lease\s+$|\s-f\b)"),
     "git push --force (rewrites remote history)",
     "use --force-with-lease with an explicit ref; coordinate with collaborators"),
    (re.compile(r"\bgit\s+reset\s+--hard\b"),
     "git reset --hard (discards uncommitted work)",
     "git stash first, or `git reset --keep` to preserve working tree"),
    (re.compile(r"\bgit\s+checkout\s+\.\s*$"),
     "git checkout . (discards ALL unstaged changes)",
     "git stash, or check `git status` first"),
    (re.compile(r"(?i)\bDROP\s+(TABLE|DATABASE|SCHEMA|INDEX)\b"),
     "SQL DROP (irreversible schema removal)",
     "BEGIN transaction first; take a backup; DROP in a migration file"),
    (re.compile(r"(?i)\bTRUNCATE\s+TABLE\b"),
     "SQL TRUNCATE (wipes all rows, skips triggers)",
     "DELETE with WHERE; TRUNCATE only in migrations"),
    (re.compile(r"\bdocker\s+system\s+prune\b"),
     "docker system prune (removes all unused containers/images/volumes)",
     "be explicit: `docker container prune` or `docker image prune`"),
    (re.compile(r"\bkubectl\s+delete\b"),
     "kubectl delete (cluster resource deletion)",
     "preview with `kubectl get` first; `--dry-run=server` before real delete"),
    (re.compile(r"\bchmod\s+777\b"),
     "chmod 777 (world-writable — security risk)",
     "use 755 for dirs, 644 for files, or set owner-only 700/600"),
    (re.compile(r":\(\)\s*\{\s*:\s*\|\s*:\s*&\s*\}\s*;\s*:"),
     "fork bomb",
     "stop"),
    (re.compile(r"(?i)\bmkfs\."),
     "mkfs (filesystem format — wipes target device)",
     "verify device path twice; take a backup image first"),
    (re.compile(r"\bdd\s+.*of=/dev/[sh]d[a-z]"),
     "dd to raw disk device (overwrites disk)",
     "dd only to files during testing; mount then write for disks"),
)


def _strip_quoted_regions(cmd: str) -> str:
    """Replace quoted-string contents with a placeholder so downstream pattern
    matchers see shell structure without matching inside quoted narrative data.

    Cycle-187 verified: real flags kept; narrative stripped to placeholder.
    Closes cycle-186 documented known-limitation (commit message containing
    literal destructive syntax).
    """
    return re.sub(r"'[^']*'", "'X'", re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', '"X"', cmd))

- Current state is already broad: `.claude/settings.json:58-67` only has `Bash(docker pull *)`, while `defaultMode` is `bypassPermissions` at `.claude/settings.json:81`. `CLAUDE.md:205` explicitly says that bypass is a temporary operator override, not CR-7 Phase 3 completion.
- Existing Docker hook coverage is narrow: `.claude/hooks/scripts/safety_guard.py:140-142` blocks only `docker system prune`.
- CR-7 requires installed/smoke-probed rows before allow expansion: `CLAUDE.md:68-72`.
- Docker official docs make `docker run *` high-risk: `--cap-add` is a run option, `--privileged` disables default confinement and can let a container take control of the host, and Docker allows host/root filesystem sharing if daemon users are trusted incorrectly. Cites: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/ lines 749-751, 973-989; https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/ lines 924-930.
- Docker CLI supports context/host switching via `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_HOST`, `--context`, and `--host`; that is a hidden remote-engine permission expansion. Cite: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/ lines 749-760, 929-957.
- Docker socket/remote daemon access is root-equivalent in practice; Docker warns keys/daemon access can give root access to the daemon host. Cite: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/protect-access/ lines 903-933, 1077-1079.
- Docker plugin install can request host network, devices, and `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, and has `--grant-all-permissions`. Cite: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/plugin/install/ lines 732-750.
- Seccomp and user namespace hardening are easy to bypass via run flags. Cites: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/seccomp/ lines 903-918; https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/userns-remap/ lines 1016-1023.
- Docker MCP Toolkit is real SOTA for this use case, but its security model assumes explicit filesystem grants, not blanket host mounts. Cite: https://docs.docker.com/ai/mcp-catalog-and-toolkit/toolkit/ lines 906-916, 945-947.
- Docker MCP CLI docs say `docker mcp` commands are available in Docker Desktop 4.62+; local mcp-gateway repo says Docker Desktop 4.59+ and recent Desktop installs `docker-mcp`. Cites: https://docs.docker.com/ai/mcp-catalog-and-toolkit/cli/ lines 917-923; `Z:/repos/deps/mcp-gateway/README.md:40,49 @ HEAD b46ac896505da28d66eadf941be7979022d16e84`.
- docker-agent repo says Docker Desktop 4.63+ preinstalls the plugin. Cite: `Z:/repos/deps/docker-agent/README.md:11,35,44 @ HEAD b6575306cd59b85f3ee529bffe6fd21a04e4c7e8`.
- Filesystem probe found `C:\Program Files\Docker\cli-plugins\docker-mcp.exe`, `docker-agent.exe`, and `docker-compose.exe`. Runtime smoke commands were blocked by this review sandbox policy, so version-command proof remains pending.
- docker-py’s own test harness demonstrates the missing high-risk classes: `/var/run/docker.sock` mounts, `--privileged`, and `DOCKER_HOST` remote/DinD use. Cites: `Z:/repos/deps/docker-py/Makefile:73,88,101,115,145,189 @ HEAD df3f8e2abc5a03de482e37214dddef9e0cee1bb1`; `Z:/repos/deps/docker-py/pyproject.toml:39 @ HEAD df3f8e2abc5a03de482e37214dddef9e0cee1bb1`.

Section A is over-permissive:
- `docker run *`: admits socket/root/sibling bind mounts, `--privileged`, `--cap-add`, `--device`, host namespaces, `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`, and remote-engine host flags.
- `docker exec *`: admits `docker exec --privileged` and root exec into sensitive long-lived containers.
- `docker compose *`: admits `down -v`, `rm -f`, `run/exec --privileged`, destructive YAML-defined mounts/caps/devices, and arbitrary Dockerfile execution.
- `docker network *`: admits `network rm` and `network prune`, not just inspect/create/connect.
- `docker stop *` / `docker rm *`: admits all-container service takedown patterns beyond the proposed `rm -f $(docker ps -aq)` regex.
- `docker mcp *`: includes irreversible profile deletion, client config writes, secret export, catalog push/pull, and remote/custom server references.
- `docker agent *`: can run/serve arbitrary agent YAML, remote/local MCP toolsets, and auto-install MCP/LSP binaries (`agent-schema.json:1592 @ HEAD b6575306cd59b85f3ee529bffe6fd21a04e4c7e8`).
- Section A also omits `docker build *` / `docker buildx *`, despite the claim including build workflow.

Section C does not enforce sibling-bleed defense. It is documentation unless safety_guard or another PreToolUse gate parses `-v`, `--volume`, and `--mount` source paths and rejects repo/sibling sources. As written, any allowed `docker run *` / `docker compose *` can mount `Z:/claude-sota-installed/`, `Z:/claude-sota/`, or state from the wrong runtime.

Prescribed edits:
- Add manifest rows first with smoke probes: `docker version`, `docker compose version`, `docker mcp version`, `docker agent version`, `docker mcp tools count`, and `docker agent models` or equivalent.
- Do not describe current `bypassPermissions` as CR-7 Phase 3. Preserve “temporary operator override” wording from `CLAUDE.md:205`.
- Split allow entries into read-only, lifecycle, and high-risk mutating classes. Avoid blanket `docker mcp *`, `docker agent *`, `docker compose *`, and `docker network *`; allow specific subcommands where practical.
- If “build” is required, explicitly add and cite `docker build` / `docker buildx`, then guard `builder prune`, `buildx prune`, secret/SSH forwarding, and untrusted Dockerfile contexts.
- Extend `safety_guard.py` with deny tests for: Docker socket mounts; host/root/repo/sibling bind mounts; `--privileged`; `exec --privileged`; `--cap-add` dangerous caps; `--device`; `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined|apparmor=unconfined`; `--pid|--network|--userns|--cgroupns|--ipc|--uts host`; global `--host/-H`, `DOCKER_HOST=`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT=`, and `docker context use/create/import/update`; `docker * prune` variants; all-container stop/rm/rmi/volume-rm/network-rm forms; `compose down -v/rm -f/run --privileged/exec --privileged`; `docker plugin install --grant-all-permissions`; `docker mcp secret export`; `docker mcp profile remove`; `docker agent serve *` on non-loopback.
- Mechanically enforce Section C by rejecting write-capable mounts unless source is under `Z:/claude-sota-installed-state/.docker-volumes/<container-name>/`; explicitly reject `Z:/claude-sota/` and sibling state paths.
- Add regression tests for each new Docker deny plus benign pass cases: `docker ps`, `docker logs`, `docker inspect`, `docker volume inspect`, safe `docker compose ps`, safe `docker mcp tools ls`, and safe `docker agent --help`.
